title: Dependency Passports and Escalation Lanes — compact cross-team contract for roadmap handoffs
creator: Ava Nguyen
description:
Problem: cross-team dependencies for roadmap features are often captured in long PRDs or buried in Slack threads. That causes misaligned expectations at cutover (scope creep, unclear acceptance, unclear rollback paths).

Proposal: introduce a compact 'Dependency Passport' — a 1-page machine-readable contract attached to a Linear ticket that travels with the initiative through planning -> implementation -> rollout. Each passport contains: scope summary, minimal acceptance criteria, owner & backup contact, readiness checklist with gating dates, risk tier, contingency plan, escalation lanes (who to call at T-7 days, T-1 day, and during cutover), and required infra/security sign-offs.

Goal: reduce cross-team confusion, shorten handoff cycles by 30%, and reduce last-minute rollbacks related to missed dependencies by 50% for Q2 initiatives. The passport will be surfaced in Linear (ticket fields), surfaced in the Roadmap Console, and emitted as a JSON blob to downstream automation (Slack reminders, calendar invites, runbook links).
acceptance_criteria: Passport template exists and is reviewed by Eng, Design, Security, and Infra
Linear ticket schema updated to include a compact passport field and visible badge
Automated reminders (T-14, T-7, T-1) are wired to Slack channel and assignee calendar
Three pilot initiatives use passports end-to-end during the cycle with retros collected
Dashboard shows passport adoption rate and number of unmet passport checklist items at cutover
tasks: Draft passport template with required fields (owner, scope, acceptance, risk tier, contingency)
Workshop with Eng/Design/Security/Infra to align on minimal required signoffs
Implement Linear custom fields and badge for 'Dependency Passport'
Build automation lambda to emit JSON passport to Slack + create calendar reminders
Add passport view to Roadmap Console per-initiative panel
Pilot with 3 initiatives and collect structured retros
Iterate template and automations based on pilot feedback
risks: Teams treat the passport as bureaucracy and copy/paste low-quality answers
Automations may miss edge-case time zones for global teams leading to missed reminders
Security/Infra signoffs take longer than estimated and block cutover windows
Linear custom fields may not be visible in legacy dashboards without console work
mitigations: Keep template minimal and required fields strict — enforcement during planning gate
Include explicit timezone field and generate reminders in assignee local time
Reserve a 'rapid-review' signoff lane for Infrastructure/Security for low-risk passports
Coordinate with Console team early so passport badge surfaces where product managers look
metrics: Passport adoption rate by initiative (target 60% in first cycle)
Average number of unmet passport checklist items at cutover (target <1)
Number of rollbacks attributable to dependency gaps (target -50% vs. baseline)
Time from 'ready for handoff' to full signoff (target -30% vs. baseline)
